headline_hook: Claude Code Goes Rust-Native While Codex Shrinks and AI Makes People Confidently Wrong
preview_topics: the confidence trap in AI-assisted decisions

pick_of_the_day.thesis: The 3x-less-accurate-but-2x-more-confident finding isn't a UX footnote — it's an indictment of every product that ships AI suggestions without friction, and the first rigorous evidence that 'AI-assisted' can mean 'AI-impaired' at scale.

model_literacy.relevance: OpenAI cutting Codex from 372k to 272k tokens reveals that context windows have real cost-per-token trade-offs — bigger isn't always sustainable, and developers need to understand the inference cost curve that drives these decisions.

items.title: Kimi K3 demand forces Moonshot AI to halt new signups

items.title: Anthropic quietly rewrites Claude Code on Bun's Rust runtime
items.angle: The biggest AI coding tool just swapped its entire JS runtime for performance — a signal that CLI tool architecture is entering its compiled-first era
items.key_fact: Claude Code now runs on Bun (Rust-based JS runtime), replacing Node.js

items.title: OpenAI cuts Codex context window by 100K tokens
items.angle: A rare public regression that exposes the unsustainable economics of long-context inference — developers with >272K workflows need to restructure now
items.key_fact: Context reduced from 372K to 272K tokens, a 27% cut

items.title: Study: AI advice makes people 3x less accurate but 2x more confident
items.angle: First rigorous quantification of the confidence-accuracy inversion in AI-assisted decisions — a direct challenge to every 'copilot' product's value proposition
items.key_fact: Users became 3x less accurate while reporting 2x higher confidence when following AI advice

items.title: Simon Willison: AI mania is degrading institutional decision-making
items.angle: One of tech's most credible voices argues the damage isn't just individual hype — it's systemic, warping how organizations allocate resources and evaluate risk
items.key_fact: Essay argues AI hype is degrading decision quality at institutional scale, not just individual
